notes: Both coders gave 'delegates' to both documents (agreement 1.0). Main disagreements: (1) modality for statements phrased as 'can/may/will' (informs vs may vs should; resolved by the verb in the source, with 'we/I will' commitments as must or informs for expected-use lists); (2) unit_stance on disclosure and consequence sentences (permit/neutral/require; resolved as require for duties to cite or reflect, prohibit for flat bans); (3) policy_type between neighbours such as P04/P09, P05/P110/P83, P36/P74/P107, P87/P02, P17/P59 (resolved by re-reading the sentence and choosing the type whose definition matches the operative content); (4) phase and actor for instructor 'My Use' statements (resolved as course-start / instructor) and for institutional statements. Matching used anchor overlap; a few greedy mismatches were re-paired by hand. Only-A/only-B units were mostly sentences one coder split from a neighbour or skipped; all but one were real statements and kept. The one dropped A-only unit was a list item inside an already coded sentence.
